## Summary (Ask Bunkankun 聞分館君)

The *Jìngmíng xuán lùn* (T1780) is an eight-fascicle treatise on the *Vimalakīrti-nirdeśa-sūtra* ([KR6i0076](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6i/KR6i0076) = T475) by the Sānlùn 三論 (Three-Treatise / Madhyamaka) master [吉藏](https://ask.bunkankun.org/Persons/%E5%90%89%E8%97%8F) Jízàng (549–623 CE). It functions as a prolegomenon to the verse-by-verse commentary [KR6i0084](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6i/KR6i0084) *Wéimó jīng yìshū* (T1781). *Jìngmíng* 淨名 ("Pure Name") is a Chinese semantic translation of *Vimalakīrti* (parallel to Xuánzàng's later *Wúgòuchēng* 無垢稱). The Taishō header cross-references Nos. 475 and 1781.

**Abstract**

Jízàng was the systematizer and final great representative of the Sānlùn school, the Chinese Madhyamaka tradition descended from [鳩摩羅什](https://ask.bunkankun.org/Persons/%E9%B3%A9%E6%91%A9%E7%BE%85%E4%BB%80) Kumārajīva via [僧肇](https://ask.bunkankun.org/Persons/%E5%83%A7%E8%82%87) Sēngzhào and [法朗](https://ask.bunkankun.org/Persons/%E6%B3%95%E6%9C%97) Fǎlǎng. The *Jìngmíng xuán lùn* is one of three major Vimalakīrti texts by Jízàng (the others being [KR6i0084](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6i/KR6i0084) *Wéimó jīng yìshū* and the lost *Wéimó luè shū*). Together they constitute the most extensive Sānlùn-school engagement with the *Vimalakīrti*.

The *Xuán lùn* (a *xuán*-genre treatise rather than a verse-by-verse *shū*) addresses the *Vimalakīrti*'s philosophical core: the doctrine of non-duality (*bùèr* 不二), the bodhisattva *upāya* (skillful means), the relation of *saṃsāra* and *nirvāṇa*, and the bodhisattva's stance toward *bodhi*. Jízàng deploys his characteristic *liángbiǎn* 兩遣 (refutation of both extremes) hermeneutic to argue that the *Vimalakīrti*'s teaching is the perfect Madhyamaka realization of *prajñā*.

Jízàng spent his late career at Yángzhōu (605–615 CE) under the Sui *Jiāngdū* 江都 establishment, before relocating to Cháng'ān at the start of the Tang. The *Xuán lùn* and *Yìshū* belong to this productive Yángzhōu period.
